classification.difficultyReason: Construct the two-dice sample space and count doubles, an overlapping event and high totals.

content.prompt: Two fair dice are rolled and the uppermost numbers are noted.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Represent the sample space by drawing an array and listing all the possible outcomes.

inlines.text: Each pair is (die 1, die 2). Rows give die 1 outcomes 1–6; columns give die 2 outcomes 1–6. All 36 outcomes are equally likely.

answer.worked:
Only $(6,6)$ is favourable among the $36$ cells.
$$P(\text{double }6)=\frac{1}{36}.$$

Count the $6$ cells in row $6$ and the $5$ other cells in column $6$. Count $(6,6)$ once.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{at least one }6)&=\frac{6+5}{36}\\P(\text{at least one }6)&=\frac{11}{36}\end{align*}$$

The favourable cells are $(4,6),(5,5),(6,4),(5,6),(6,5),(6,6)$, giving totals $10,11$ or $12$.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{total}\geq10)&=\frac{6}{36}\\P(\text{total}\geq10)&=\frac{1}{6}\end{align*}$$
